snippet: After an FDA advisory committee voted 9-3 on Wednesday against recommending Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cardiomyopathy drug for approval, stakeholders allege an “ulterior motive” and “biased intentions.”

title: Lilly and Resilience invest $750M in diabetes and obesity drug device supply
snippet: The investment will expand Resilience’s U.S. capacity to make the KwikPen device Eli Lilly uses to deliver its injectable diabetes and obesity medicines.

title: AbbVie shares pressured as Q2 I&I beat falls below investor expectations
snippet: AbbVie investors’ sky-high expectations led to a 4% share decline on Friday as the company reported more modest consensus beats than expected.

title: Novo's IL-6 inhibitor fails in cardiovascular Phase 3, plunging shares more than 9%
snippet: Novo Nordisk's IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab failed to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in the late-stage trial, dashing hopes for an edge in the hyper-competitive cardiometabolic space.

title: Moderna maintains 10% growth target despite Phase 3 norovirus miss
snippet: Moderna’s norovirus vaccine failed in a Phase 3 trial, but the company still has faith in an ambitious revenue growth target thanks to ex-U.S. vaccine sales and a unanimous FDA adcomm win for mFLUSIVA.

title: Alnylam absorbs $10.8B blowback after cutting full-year guidance for TTR franchise
snippet: Alnylam’s revenue cut “may create a near term credibility overhang and could “raise questions on peak sales potential, even if there’s tailwinds in the competitive landscape,” according to Stifel.

title: UniQure welcomes possible adcomm for Huntington’s asset as regulatory ‘jitters’ spread through biopharma
snippet: UniQure is ready to put its Huntington’s disease gene therapy through an advisory committee meeting—even as the broader rare disease space has been put on edge by recent FDA scrutiny of assets by Replimune and Capricor.

title: Replimune overcomes ‘messy data’ to secure positive adcomm vote for melanoma therapy
snippet: The FDA’s Cellular, Tissue and Gene Therapies advisory committee voted 10 to 3 in favor of Replimune’s immunotherapy for advanced melanoma in combination with Bristol Myers Squibb’s Opdivo, but trial design was a major sticking point as the panel deliberated.

title: BMS’ ‘big beat’ clouded by Cobenfy, heart disease data delays
snippet: Strong quarterly results are prompting Bristol Myers Squibb to lift its 2026 outlook, though the company is facing another delay for key Cobenfy Alzheimer’s data and a pushed-back readout for milvexian.

title: Regeneron’s ‘aversion’ to M&A questioned as bumper Q2 builds war chest
snippet: Calls for Regeneron to step up dealmaking have intensified as the company has established an $18 billion cash pile and suffered clinical trial setbacks.

title: Daiichi’s pipeline falls behind rivals as cash flow nears peak: analysts
snippet: With Enhertu and Datroway hitting their peak revenue and rivals flowing into the antibody-drug conjugate space, Jefferies cuts expectations for Daiichi Sankyo.

title: J&J secures right to take the helm in up to $925M Sail CAR T pact
snippet: As part of the collaboration, Johnson & Johnson will have an exclusive option to acquire Sail Biomedicines for an additional $2.58 billion.

title: Sanofi’s new CEO wants more ‘realistic view’ of Phase 3 go/no-go decisions
snippet: Sanofi is going to "look very deeply" at its late-stage pipeline as part of a portfolio prioritization initiative, though new CEO Belén Garijo didn’t commit to shelving a specific number of assets.

title: Life after the lead asset: Advancing an early-stage pipeline
snippet: In this episode of Denatured presented by Arvinas, Jennifer Smith-Parker speaks to Arvinas President and CEO Randy Teel about the strategic discipline and leadership required to successfully refocus a company on an early-stage pipeline after a lead asset is outlicensed, discontinued or otherwise falls away.

title: New funding, new jobs: 4 biotechs hiring after series B raises
snippet: Biotechs that announced series B financing this year and are looking for employees as they grow include one that received over $100 million and another that has a partnership with a Big Pharma company.

title: Not-so-special delivery: When biopharmas fumble layoff news
snippet: So far in 2026, over 50 biopharmas have cut or plan to cut their workforces. If they didn’t take a careful, thoughtful approach to telling people they were being laid off, they likely left a negative impression on employees, based on stories shared with BioSpace.

title: Biogen validated the Alzheimer’s tau theory. CEO Viehbacher still isn’t betting the store
snippet: With so many unknowns, Biogen is carefully eyeing its next-gen Alzheimer’s treatment diranersen as a high-risk, high-reward project with the potential for a major payout around 2030.

title: FDA advisers vote against approval of Capricor’s DMD therapy in chaotic adcomm meeting
snippet: During a perplexing advisory committee meeting in which FDA reviewers focused largely on the Phase 3 HOPE-3 trial’s secondary endpoint of cardiac function, experts pointed to “very fragile” data. The committee voted 9-3 against approval of deramiocel.

title: Private biotechs Caldera and Vidya raise $478M collectively in reverse go-public mergers

title: Biogen shifts M&A strategy as Apellis acquisition pushes revenue above analyst expectations

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode

title: Lilly just bought renowned regulator Peter Marks a pipeline to play with
